newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor says Vietnam plan still on.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor says Vietnam plan still on.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co said on Monday its planned joint venture in Vietnam was still on despite remarks by a high-ranking Hanoi government official that Vietnam's Prime Minister was not in favour of granting a licence.
"We don't believe the remarks were the Vietnamese government's official stance. The plan is still on," said Lee Jun-ha, a manager at Hyundai's public information department.
Vietnam's Vice Minister for Industry Nguyen Xuan Chuan told Reuters on Monday "the prime minister is not in favour of the Hyundai project, he wants to decline it."
Hyundai's Lee said: "We expected the licence to be given before the end of 1996, but have not received yet. But we don't believe it means our plan had been rejected."

A senior official at Vietnam's Ministry of Planning and Investment had said last month that the approval for the roughly $250 million project with the Interior Ministry would be granted before the end of 1996.
